newsitem.title: UK: National Express yr pretax profits up 45 pct.
newsitem.headline: National Express yr pretax profits up 45 pct.

text.p: Transport group National Express Group Plc announced a 45 percent jump in annual profits on Thursday, boosted by its move onto Britain's railways, under the controversial privatisation of the former British Rail passenger network.

Pretax profits rose to 60.1 million pounds ($96.3 million) last year from 41.5 million in 1995 on sales up 51 percent at 482.5 million pounds. The year's total dividend payout was increased 1.5 pence to 11.5p on earnings up 17.5 percent at 32.8 pence.

The bus and coach operator's first two British train operating franchises, Gatwick Express and Midland Mainline, made 2.097 million pounds in operating profits on 108.48 million pounds of income last year. The firm said it increased passenger traffic on Midland Mainline by nine percent and promised further "new fares, products and promotions" to increase demand further.
Traffic on Gatwick Express, which operates the fast rail link between central London and Gatwick airport saw a three percent increase in passenger numbers last year.

The company has now been awarded a further three of the 25 regional franchises which were on offer under the privatisation programme -- Scotrail, Central Trains and North London Railways, making it one of the nation's biggest rail service operators.

"The highlight of 1996 has been the rapid development of the group's train services," chairman Michael Davies said in his results statement."National Express has put considerable effort into bidding sensibly for franchises in the UK rail privatisation, and the first two franchises...performed extremely well and contributed to the Group's results ahead of expectations."
"The current year has started well, with all businesses performing satisfactorily, and we are looking forward to another year of growth and development."

Operating profits at the company's bus division jumped 59 percent to 39.4 million pounds on sales of 175.59 million pounds, boosted by further acquisitions. The Express Coaches division made an operating profit of 10.48 million pounds on sales of 169.87 million pounds while its East Midlands Airport in Britain made 10.3 million pounds on turnover of 28.62 million pounds. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
